key_insight: The paper gives an explicit finite-iteration bound for exact data-driven inverse optimization of integer linear programs by turning an abstract geometric convergence rate into a problem-size-dependent iteration guarantee.
engineering_relevance: This makes inverse modeling for ILP-based decision systems more predictable and deployable, since practitioners can estimate how much computation is needed to recover weights from observed optimal decisions.
method: Uses projected subgradient descent on the suboptimality loss for inverse optimization.
Derives an explicit lower bound on the geometric constant b3(ll_sub) in terms of sample size, feature dimension, feature ranges, and constraint-matrix structure.
Converts the previously implicit O(1/b3(ll_sub)^2) iteration bound into a fully explicit complexity bound up to polynomial factors in standard constants.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical complexity result for ILP inverse optimization, showing exact consistency can be achieved in finitely many oracle iterations with an explicit bound derived from problem parameters.
watch_item: The bound is explicit only up to polynomial factors in constants such as weight-set diameter, step size, and Lipschitz constant, so practical runtime can still depend strongly on these choices and on ILP structure.
paper_title: Explicit Iteration Complexity of Exact Data-Driven Inverse Optimization for Integer Linear Programs
